text.p: Brazil's Banco Excel Economico and U.S. insurer Cigna Corp. on Thursday announced a joint venture to strenghten their position in one of the fastest-growing insurance markets in Latin America.

With initial capital of 20 million reais, the new company, to be called Excel Cigna Seguradora SA, will sell life and accident insurance plans in Brazil, where the insurance market is expected to grow between 14 percent and 18 percent annually in coming years.
"The potential growth of the insurance business here is enormous," said Ezequiel Nasser, president of Banco Excel Economico.

Most of optimism for future growth reflects the success of Brazil's anti-inflation drive, which has increased the population's purchasing power and allowed Brazilians to save money and make long-term investments.
Nasser said the Brazilian insurance sector accounted for only two percent of the country's gross domestic product, compared with a global average of five percent.
"That shows how we can grow," he said.

The new insurer plans to snap up at least two percent of the local insurance market, which last year was estimated at 15 billion reais. The company expects revenues of $40 million to $50 million in its first year of operations. Its aim is to rank among the country's 10 largest insurers within 10 years.
Under the terms of the deal, Cigna will become a shareholder of Banco Excel Economico, with the acquisition of a 4.6 percent stake in the private bank.
Cigna, which is joining Switzerland's Union Bancaire Privee (UBP) as a foreign shareholder of Excel Economico, will pay $48 million for the shares, the Brazilian bank said.

"The bank is run by a great group of people. It is changing the way banking is made in Brazil," Cigna International President Kingsley Schubert said, explaining why the U.S. company decided to take part in the venture.
"It was easy to talk with Excel Economico because we are both aggressive. We want to provide cost-effective products and good services to clients," Schubert said.
Cigna's total investment amounts to $78 million, including the premium it will pay for using Excel's branch network, investment in training and technology.
Despite the joint venture with Cigna, Excel Economico said it would stand by agreements with local companies to offer car insurance and pension and health plans.
Meanwhile, Cigna said it would maintain its Brazilian unit focusing on property insurance.
Cigna is among the 10 largest insurers in the United States, managing $100 billion in assets and with a net worth of about $8 billion.
Banco Excel Economico is one of Brazil's 20 biggest banks, with more than $3.0 billion in assets and 900,000 clients.
